subject: JAX-RTM kickoff — gradient-based retrieval for assimilation
body: Team — kickoff for JAX-RTM in graphs-retrieval. From our release: a fully JAX-differentiable radiative transfer model solver for satellite simulation and meteorological data assimilation, with a calibrated physical solver for cloud and ice microphysics. Differentiability is the product: gradients let us optimize cloud properties — ice water content, effective radius, spatial alignment — directly against satellite observations, on TPU/GPU. The customer is the assimilation-pipeline collaboration; today their retrievals are lookup-table based and they want gradient-based retrieval. Milestones: environment plus the required Ping Yang ice-crystal single-scattering database (155 MB) set up and forward simulations validated by April 17; a gradient-based retrieval demo against real satellite observations by end of May; scale/production decision by end of June (window closes July 6). Jelena owns staffing; the budget conversation with Finance is mine. — Anders
